subject: Post-call: clarifying p95/p99 latency & streaming expectations
messages:
From: Anika Rao <sre-lead@veridianhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up on latency & streaming targets — call recap

Hi Grace + Ben,

Thanks for carving time today. High-level recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can get a concrete MA P (mutual action plan) in place: 

- Goal: move inference from IncumbentAI to Redwood Hosted for Veridian's triage assistant by end of Q3.
- Production workload: ~120 req/s peak during business hours; average 35 req/s; 1–3k tokens per request (model context + user history).
- Critical SLOs we need validated end-to-end (client -> your hosted API -> model -> response): p95 <= 220 ms, p99 <= 420 ms for single-stream responses when concurrency <= 50.
- Streaming requirement: client-side needs partial token streaming for low-latency UX; we need first-token < 80 ms median and steady per-token streaming while response streams out.
- Fallbacks: we expect automatic fallback to a slightly lower-cost model if our SLOs cannot be met for sustained periods.

Clarifying questions:
1) Do you have prior hosted benchmarks for long-context (1k–3k tokens) p95/p99 under streaming for 50 concurrency? If so, can you share representative traces or a summary?
2) What tooling will Redwood provide so we can run side-by-side synthetic E2E tests (we want the test harness to exercise our client multiplexing, streaming, and KV-cache hit assumptions)?
3) Any observable differences we should expect when comparing Redwood Hosted vs our current provider (IncumbentAI) re: head-of-line latency during spikes?

I'll loop in our infra lead if you need logs or request traces from IncumbentAI. For next steps we want a short mutual test plan + timeline so procurement can schedule capacity.

Thanks,
Anika Rao
SRE Lead, Platform
Veridian Health

--
Attachment: incident-sample-traces.zip (stub)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anika Rao <sre-lead@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on latency & streaming targets — call recap

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear summary, and great call today. Couple of quick answers and a proposed MA P to validate the numbers you quoted.

Short answers:
- We do have hosted benchmarks for long-context streaming but want to validate them against your exact request distribution and token sizes. Our internal long-context p95/p99 numbers (hosted, dedicated runs) for a comparable model family are typically in the 180–240 ms p95 and 380–480 ms p99 band at concurrency 40–60 for single-stream responses, but those are sensitive to batch/coalescing settings and prefix cache behavior.
- We can provide a Redwood test harness (config + k6 script + a small client shim) that drives both standard request/streaming flows and KV-cache warmup. I'll attach a reference YAML and an hypothesis matrix to get started.
- Head-of-line during spikes: our hosted runtime uses continuous batching + smart routing; you'll see slightly lower variance vs naive endpoints but p99 tail can still move during sustained overload if concurrency and batch windows collide. We'll include a gating plan in the MA P.

Proposed mutual action plan (timeline goal: 3 weeks to initial acceptance testing):
1) Today–2 business days: exchange traces + representative payloads (you already shared the sample traces — thanks).
2) Redwood provides test harness + recommended config (p95/p99 hypothesis matrix, streaming window settings) — target delivery 48 hours.
3) Veridian runs side-by-side synthetic E2E tests against IncumbentAI and Redwood Hosted using the harness; we offer a short dedicated test window with tokenized logs.
4) Joint analysis call to review results, adjust config, and agree on acceptance criteria.

Action items for us: 
- I'll attach the YAML harness and a short spreadsheet mapping expected p95/p99 deltas and test vectors.
- Ben and Marcus will scope a short hosted test window and supply a temporary API key and capacity reservation for your testing.

Would you like us to provision the reserved test window for a morning or afternoon slot next week?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood-test-harness-config.yaml (stub), p95-p99-hypothesis-matrix.xlsx (stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 14:55:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on latency & streaming targets — call recap

Thanks Grace — quick internal note on the test plan and our responsibilities.

- I'll book a 4-hour reserved test window on our hosted cluster for next Tue (2027-07-27) 1400–1800 UTC; respond if Veridian prefers a different time.
- Marcus: please pre-warm KV cache profiles for the models listed in the spreadsheet and set concurrency throttles so we can run clean p95/p99 measurements (no noisy neighbor artifacts).
- I'll generate a short script to capture first-byte latency for streaming and token-level deltas; needs a lightweight client shim from Veridian to run locally.

Also noting: we should confirm their encryption/KMS expectations for the test logs; if they need non-prod keys we can accommodate but procurement will require a quick DPA addendum.

Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anika Rao <sre-lead@veridianhealth.com>, ops@veridianhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 01:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on latency & streaming targets — call recap

Thanks Anika — looping back with concrete next steps so procurement and infra can act: 

1) Test window: we've reserved Tue 2027-07-27 14:00–18:00 UTC (4 hours). If that doesn't work, propose one alternative and we'll rebook.
2) Deliverables from Redwood (by end of day Thu):
   - redwood-test-harness-config.yaml (attached) — includes: request mix, token-size buckets, streaming client shim instructions, and KV-cache warmup steps.
   - p95-p99-hypothesis-matrix.xlsx (attached) — expected bands and pass/fail thresholds for p95/p99, first-byte streaming targets.
   - short Doc with acceptance criteria and what constitutes a rollback (fallback conditions). Link to HubSpot test plan below.
3) Action for Veridian:
   - Share representative client multiplexing config and any rate-limiting/proxy behavior that could affect head-of-line latency.\   - Confirm if you require logs encrypted with your KMS for the test artifacts.

Attachments (sent): redwood-test-harness-config.yaml, p95-p99-hypothesis-matrix.xlsx
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/7893, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_example_testplan

If we agree on the window and deliverables I'll send the temporary test API key and a short runbook for the window.

Best regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
